Unobtrusive

un-ub-TROO-siv · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unobtrusive is not conspicuous or attracting attention; discreetly blending into the background.

She chose an unobtrusive gray sedan instead of the flashy red sports car, preferring not to stand out in the parking lot.

Worked Example

The museum's unobtrusive lighting was designed to illuminate each painting without ever drawing attention to the fixtures themselves.

Unobtrusive doesn't mean invisible -- it means deliberately understated, so it doesn't pull focus away from what actually matters.

How Unobtrusive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

understated

understated: not showy; deliberately downplayed

low-key

low-key: modest and not attracting attention

Antonyms

conspicuous

conspicuous: clearly visible; attracting notice

showy

showy: very noticeable; designed to attract attention

How Strong Is It? — modest → invisible → unobtrusive

modest vs. unobtrusive

modest vs. unobtrusive: Modest just means not showy, without unobtrusive's stronger sense of being specifically designed to escape notice.

invisible vs. unobtrusive

invisible vs. unobtrusive: Invisible takes the idea of not being noticed to its literal extreme -- truly unseen, not just easy to overlook.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — un-

prefix — un-: not (English)

root — trudere

root — trudere: to thrust, push (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Unobtrusive combines un- ('not') with obtrusive, from Latin ob- ('against') plus trudere ('to thrust, push') -- something obtrusive pushes itself into notice, so something unobtrusive does the opposite.

Use the root in a new word: intrude

Use the root in a new word: intrude: It felt rude to intrude on their private conversation, so she waited quietly until they finished.
